messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT ALERT — autoscale surge triggered multiple serving runtime failures in eu-west-1 (OOMs + container crashloops). Pager routed to @pranav (oncall).

pranav: I’m on it. seeing huge scale-up between 14:02 and 14:05, nodes rapidly added then evicted. can ppl avoid mass deploys?

sasha: we didn't deploy. traffic spike from a single customer job hitting long sequences. traces show many requests with seq_len ~ 10k.

jamie: logs from runtime: ```
E tensorflow: Allocator (GPU_0_bfc) ran out of memory trying to allocate 2.1GiB
W serving: kv_cache miss storm; concurrent contexts > 600
container: exit code 137 (OOM)
```

lee: CPU on nodes is fine, it's CUDA memory. autoscaler saw high pending pods -> spun up more GPU nodes -> warmup blowout, more requests routed -> more OOMs. classic feedback loop.

maya: customer-impact: partial brownout for EU region. 10-15% of requests returned 502 / timeouts since 14:03. engineering and SEs notified.

pranav: immediate mitigation plan: 1) throttle incoming long-sequence requests via gateway (rate-limit/size cap) 2) apply autoscaler damping to avoid aggressive scaling 3) restart a subset of serving pools pinned to smaller batch sizes 4) roll out fallback model (smaller quantized) for burst traffic.

opsbot: Command accepted: `postmortem: create incident/3751234567`

sasha: Gateway patch ready. Pushing size cap rule now: `if seq_len > 2048 -> 429 (ask to retry with resumable chunking)`

jamie: Patching now on prod edge: `curl -X POST https://gateway/flags -d '{"max_seq_len":2048}'` (running canary on 3 edge hosts)

lee: autoscaler update: `kubectl -n runtime patch hpa inference-autoscaler --type=json -p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/behavior","value":{"scaleUp":{"policies":[{"type":"Pods","value":1,"periodSeconds":60}],"stabilizationWindowSeconds":300}}}]'` -> adds strong damping. Applying to eu-west pools.

pranav: also setting max surge for rollout to 0 to avoid churn causing more restarts.

maya: Noting customer comms: SEs sending templated note: short-term degraded throughput in EU, mitigation in progress, ETA 30-45m for stable fallback routing.

sasha: Implemented gateway cap. traffic to long sequences is dropping -> immediate error rate for OOMs decreasing from 18% -> 6%.

jamie: Restarting runtime pools with `SERVED_BATCH_SIZE=8` and `KV_CACHE_ENABLED=false` for canary nodes. rolling restart in progress (3/12).

opsbot: Deployment event: `runtime-pool-eu-1 restart` by jamie — status: started.

lee: Observability: token-level latency telemetry shows p95 down from 1.2s to 800ms on canary after reduced batch sizes. but capacity per GPU decreased, so throughput lower.

pranav: tradeoff accepted — prefer steady throughput over crashloops. keep autoscaler damped until behaviour stabilizes.

sasha: I’m enabling fallback route: requests tagged with high seq_len -> route to `small-quant` model variant (half memory). patching routing table now.

jamie: Routing change applied. small-quant serving pools healthy. error rate in EU now ~2.1%, latency stabilized.

maya: Customer impact update: 70% of affected requests now served by fallback; remaining 30% are either retried or rejected with 429. SEs to continue outreach for high-priority customers.

pranav: next steps (short): 1) keep autoscaler damping for 30m 2) leave gateway cap live for 1h 3) schedule follow-up to tune binpacking & batch_size heuristics 4) collect traces for offending customer job and ask them to paginate/stream.

lee: logs for one crash event (for reference): ```
[2026-03-14T14:04:11Z] worker-7 PID 2481 CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY at allocate.cu:58
[2026-03-14T14:04:11Z] container terminated with code 137, OOM-killer invoked
[2026-03-14T14:04:12Z] kubelet: evicting pod runtime-eu-7 due to memory pressure
```

sasha: note: autoscaler metrics misinterpreted short-term concurrency as sustained demand; we should feed sequence-length histogram into scaler to avoid this. filed ticket INF-7321.

opsbot: Ticket created: INF-7321 — "incorporate seq_length signal into autoscaler" (linked to incident).

jamie: we should also add quick throttle hook at model serving to cap concurrent contexts per GPU (eg 200). drafting change.

pranav: oncall handoff in 30m. if stable for next 20m, i'll mark incident as mitigated and hand to day SRE. otherwise I stay on.

maya: Communicating to customers: short note sent to impacted customer cohort, status updated on status.redwood.ai, and SEs have a list of affected orgs.

lee: monitoring: watchlist created: `eu-serving-ooms`, `eu-autoscale-oscillation`, `eu-fallback-ratio`. alerts reduced from page -> warning after mitigation.

pranav: current status: mitigated -> partial brownout removed, fallback active, autoscaler damped. assigning follow-ups: INF-7321 (autoscale), INF-7322 (gateway fragment/size-capping), INF-7323 (batch heuristics).

sasha: thanks all. great quick coordination. :thumbsup:

pranav: closing notes for now — will attach logs and timeline to postmortem. if anyone wants additional metrics slices ping me.

incident-bot: Incident status changed: MAJOR -> MITIGATED.

maya: leaving this thread open for postmortem notes.
